arxiv-1805-04966.title: On the k k -partition dimension of graphs
arxiv-1805-04966.creator: Alejandro Estrada-Moreno
arxiv-1805-04966.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Alejandro Estrada-Moreno. As a generalization of the concept of the partition dimension of a graph, this article introduces the notion of the k k -partition dimension. Given a nontrivial connected graph G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) , a partition Π \Pi of V V is said to be a k k -partition generator of G G if any pair of different vertices u , v ∈ V u,v\in V is distinguished by at least k k vertex sets of Π \Pi

arxiv-2012-03786.creator: Jack Bowden, Björn Bornkamp, Ekkehard Glimm, & Frank Bretz

arxiv-2111-11000.title: PRISM: A Hierarchical Intrusion Detection Architecture for Large-Scale Cyber Networks
arxiv-2111-11000.creator: Yahya Javed, Mosab A. Khayat, Ali A. Elghariani, and Arif Ghafoor
arxiv-2111-11000.description: Abstract The increase in scale of cyber networks and the rise in sophistication of cyber-attacks have introduced several challenges in intrusion detection. The primary challenge is the requirement to detect complex multi-stage attacks in realtime by processing the immense amount of traffic produced by present-day networks.

arxiv-2302-11671.title: Asymptotic Ultraviolet-safe Unification of Gauge and Yukawa Couplings: The exceptional case
arxiv-2302-11671.creator: Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Aldo Deandrea, Roman Pasechnik, Zhi-Wei Wang
arxiv-2302-11671.description: Abstract The ultimate dream of unification models consists in combining both gauge and Yukawa couplings into one unified coupling. This is achieved by using a supersymmetric exceptional E 6 {\rm E}_{6} gauge symmetry together with asymptotic unification in compact five-dimensional space-time.

arxiv-2403-00305.title: Discovery of Asymmetric Spike-like Structures of the 10 au Disk around the Very Low-luminosity Protostar Embedded in the Taurus Dense Core MC 27/L1521F with ALMA astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , CASA ( CASA Team et al. 2022 )
arxiv-2403-00305.creator: Kazuki Tokuda, Naoto Harada, Mitsuki Omura, Tomoaki Matsumoto, Toshikazu Onishi, Kazuya Saigo, Ayumu Shoshi, Shingo Nozaki, Kengo Tachihara, Naofumi Fukaya, Yasuo Fukui, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka, Masahiro N. Machida
arxiv-2403-00305.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kazuki Tokuda, Naoto Harada, Mitsuki Omura, Tomoaki Matsumoto, Toshikazu Onishi, Kazuya Saigo, Ayumu Shoshi, Shingo Nozaki, Kengo Tachihara, Naofumi Fukaya, Yasuo Fukui, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka, Masahiro N. Machida. Recent Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations have revealed an increasing number of compact protostellar disks with radii of less than a few tens of au and that young Class 0/I objects have an intrinsic size diversity.

arxiv-2406-00726.title: Versatile Braiding of Non-Hermitian Topological Edge States
arxiv-2406-00726.creator: Bofeng Zhu, Qiang Wang, You Wang, Qi Jie Wang, Y. D. Chong
arxiv-2406-00726.description: Abstract Among the most intriguing features of non-Hermitian (NH) systems is the ability of complex energies to form braids under parametric variation. Several braiding behaviors, including link and knot formation, have been observed in experiments on synthetic NH systems, such as looped optical fibers.

arxiv-2502-14018.title: Ultrametric Cluster Hierarchies: I Want ‘em All!
arxiv-2502-14018.creator: Andrew Draganov, Pascal Weber, Rasmus Jørgensen Anna Beer Claudia Plant Ira Assent
arxiv-2502-14018.description: Abstract Hierarchical clustering is a powerful tool for exploratory data analysis, organizing data into a tree of clusterings from which a partition can be chosen. This paper generalizes these ideas by proving that, for any reasonable hierarchy, one can optimally solve any center-based clustering objective over it (such as k k -means).

arxiv-2504-03287.title: Towards Effective EU E-Participation: The Development of AskThePublic
arxiv-2504-03287.creator: Kilian Sprenkamp, Nils Messerschmidt, Amir Sartipi, Igor Tchappi, Xiaohui Wu, Liudmila Zavolokina, Gilbert Fridgen
arxiv-2504-03287.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kilian Sprenkamp, Nils Messerschmidt, Amir Sartipi, Igor Tchappi, Xiaohui Wu, Liudmila Zavolokina, Gilbert Fridgen. E-participation platforms can be an important asset for governments in increasing trust and fostering democratic societies. By engaging non-governmental and private institutions, domain experts, and even the general public, policymakers can make informed and inclusive decisions. Drawing on the Media Richness Theory and applying the Design Science Research method, we explore how a chatbot can be designed to improve the effectiveness of the policy-making process of existing citizen involvement platforms.

arxiv-2506-02879.title: Distributed Retraction-Free and Communication-Efficient Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold
arxiv-2506-02879.creator: Yilong Song, Peijin Li, Bin Gao, Kun Yuan
arxiv-2506-02879.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yilong Song, Peijin Li, Bin Gao, Kun Yuan. Optimization problems on the Stiefel manifold, ranging from principal component analysis to enhancing neural network robustness, are ubiquitous in machine learning. The Landing algorithm avoids computationally expensive retraction operations on manifolds, making it highly competitive for large-scale problems. This paper extends this method to distributed settings, introducing EF-Landing , the first retraction-free and communication-efficient algorithm for distributed stochastic optimization on the Stiefel manifold.

arxiv-2506-11417.title: Stop learning it all to mitigate visual hallucination, Focus on the hallucination target.
arxiv-2506-11417.creator: Dokyoon Yoon,Youngsook Song, Woomyong ParkSIONIC AI dokyoon, song, max@sionic.ai
arxiv-2506-11417.description: Abstract Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) frequently suffer from hallucination issues, generating information about objects that are not present in input images during vision-language tasks. These hallucinations particularly undermine model reliability in practical applications requiring accurate object identification. To address this challenge, we propose TL-DPO, a preference learning approach that mitigates hallucinations by focusing on targeted areas where they occur.

arxiv-2506-21890.title: Kinetic theories: from curved space to flat space
arxiv-2506-21890.creator: Shu Lin
arxiv-2506-21890.description: Abstract We show how to map kinetic theories for spinning particles in curved space to flat space through choice of inertial frame that eliminate forces acting on momentum and spin, thus putting the idea of mimicking off-equilibrium state by metric perturbation to equilibrium state on firm ground. The equivalence has been shown for hydrodynamic and elastic regimes.

arxiv-2510-22872.title: Dirac Equation and Representation Dependent Scattering Phenomena
arxiv-2510-22872.creator: Muhammad Adeel Ajaib
arxiv-2510-22872.description: Abstract We show that spin-flip probabilities emerge in the relativistic regime for scalar potentials, absent in the standard Dirac representation. We examine 1D scattering for the Dirac equation employing an alternate matrix representation introduced by the Author in an earlier study.

arxiv-2512-17711.title: Reconstructing Pre-Satellite Tropical Cyclogenesis Climatology Using Deep Learning
arxiv-2512-17711.creator: Chanh Kieu, Thanh T.N. Nguyen, Duc-Trong Le, Duc Gia-Anh Hoang, Quang-Lap Luu, Binh T. Dang, Truong X. Ngo, Quang-Trung Luu, Tien D. Du, Khiem V. Mai
arxiv-2512-17711.description: Abstract A reliable tropical cyclone (TC) climatology is the key to assessing historical and future changes in TC activities. While global TC records have been systematically maintained since the early 1940s, substantial uncertainties remain for the pre-satellite era during which TC observations relied mostly on scattered aircraft reconnaissance and sporadic ship reports.

pmc-10609390.title: Ticks and Chlamydia-Related Bacteria in Swiss Zoological Gardens Compared to in Contiguous and Distant Control Areas
pmc-10609390.creator: Vincent Vanat, Sébastien Aeby, Gilbert Greub, Pat Nuttall
pmc-10609390.description: Ticks are vectors of numerous agents of medical importance and may be infected by various Chlamydia-related bacteria, such as members of Parachlamydiaceae and Rhabdochlamydiaceae families, which are sharing the same biphasic life cycle with the pathogenic Chlamydia. However, the veterinary importance of ticks and of their internalized pathogens remains poorly studied.

pmc-11356154.title: The Galvanic Corrosion of AM60B Coupled with DC01 in Simulated Environments with Varying Water Salinity
pmc-11356154.creator: Wei Zhang, Chuntang Yu, Wanqi Pu, Xiaoyun Li, Chi Zhang, Renju Cheng, Guozheng Quan, Linlin Yang, Fuhui Wang
pmc-11356154.description: The galvanic corrosion performance of AM60B coupled to DC01 was characterized in simulated environments with varying water salinity. The results showed that the coupled DC01 effectively accelerated the corrosion rate of AM60B, and the increased salt concentration had a significant effect on the deterioration process.

pmc-11428208.title: Structure-based validation of recombinant light-harvesting complex II
pmc-11428208.creator: Soichiro Seki, Tomoko Miyata, Naoko Norioka, Hideaki Tanaka, Genji Kurisu, Keiichi Namba, Ritsuko Fujii, Gerhard Hummer
pmc-11428208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Light-harvesting complex II (LHCII) captures sunlight and dissipates excess energy to drive photosynthesis. To elucidate this mechanism, the individual optical properties of pigments in the LHCII protein must be identified. In vitro reconstitution with apoproteins synthesized by Escherichia coli and pigment–lipid mixtures from natural sources is an effective approach; however, the local environment surrounding each pigment within reconstituted LHCII (rLHCII) has only been indirectly estimated using spectroscopic and biochemical methods.

pmc-11504713.title: Effects of Anesthesia with Pentobarbital/Ketamine on Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pore Opening and Ischemic Brain Damage
pmc-11504713.creator: Evelina Rekuviene, Laima Ivanoviene, Vilmante Borutaite, Ramune Morkuniene, Yong Zhao
pmc-11504713.description: Background and Objective: The alteration of mitochondrial functions, especially the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP), has been proposed as a key mechanism in the development of lesions in cerebral ischemia, wherefore it is considered as an important target for drugs against ischemic injury.

pmc-11529738.title: Assessing the relative efficacy of components of opioid-free anaesthesia in adult surgical patients: protocol for a systematic review and component network meta-analysis
pmc-11529738.creator: Amparo Belltall, Guido Mazzinari, Aisling Ní Eochagáin, Tom Wall, Ary Serpa Neto, Oscar Diaz-Cambronero, Daniel Sessler, Donal J Buggy, Juan Cata, Markus W Hollmann
pmc-11529738.description: IntroductionThe rise of opioid-free anaesthesia (OFA) aims to reduce postoperative pain while reducing opioid-related side effects during surgery. However, the various adjuvant agents used in OFA complicate the evaluation of their effectiveness and risks. Recent reviews question the clinical benefits of OFA, highlighting the need for thorough evaluation.

pmc-11699105.title: Thermotolerance screening of Brassica carinata genotypes using in vitro seed germination assay
pmc-11699105.creator: Leelawattie Persaud, Naflath Thenveettil, Ramdeo Seepaul, Bisoondat Macoon, Krishna N. Reddy, Kambham Raja Reddy
pmc-11699105.description: Temperature is a fundamental factor influencing the processes of seed germination. Investigating the response of carinata to thermal stress and establishing a dependable and efficient method for screening thermotolerance will enhance breeding programs and model applications. We assessed the response of 12 carinata genotypes to a range of eight temperatures, spanning from 8 to 37 °C, throughout the germination process.

pmc-12435807.title: Indication, technical considerations, and outcome of remote central cannulation for repeat extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: a case report
pmc-12435807.creator: Enrico Danzer, Sabrina J. Flohr, Holly L. Hedrick, Geoffrey L. Bird, Jonathan M. Chen, Natalie E. Rintoul
pmc-12435807.description: Repeat extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is rare in children with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Improving our understanding of the potential survival benefits, complications, and surgical challenges associated with this procedure is essential for enhancing decision-making regarding multicourse ECMO in CDH.

pmc-12571545.title: Effects of fractional inspired O2 on the O2 pathway during submaximal and maximal exercise in male endurance athletes
pmc-12571545.creator: Elias Lehtonen, Dominique D Gagnon, Antti‐Pekka E Rissanen, Tom Mikkola, Juha E Peltonen
pmc-12571545.description: We utilized non‐invasive methods and novel computational approaches to examine the effects of acutely varying fractional inspired O2 (FIO2) on convective and diffusive steps of O2 transport and muscle tissue (de)oxygenation during incremental cycling to exhaustion in 10 Tier 3 and 4 endurance athletes breathing either 0.152, 0.209, or 0.298 FIO2.

pmc-12696051.title: A quality framework for cryopreserved rodent disease models: INFRAFRONTIER quality principles in EMMA archiving and distribution
pmc-12696051.creator: Hilke Ehlich, Andrew Blease, Reva Biju, Montse Gustems, Fei Song, Sabine Fessele, Marzia Massimi, Konstantinos Bozonelos, Vasileios Ntafis, Anniina E. Hiltunen, Susan Marschall, Claudia Stoeger, Zuzana Khorshidi, Abdelmalek Ziadi, Karine Jambou, Arsenio Armagno, Ferdinando Scavizzi, Marcello Raspa,
pmc-12696051.description: Ensuring the quality and reproducibility of biological resources is essential for advancing biomedical research and upholding animal welfare standards. The European Mouse Mutant Archive (EMMA), part of the INFRAFRONTIER research infrastructure, plays a key role in this effort by cryopreserving scientifically validated mutant mouse and rat strains and making them accessible to the global scientific community.

pmc-12706970.title: The effect of seasonal and meteorological factors on suicide rates in the Lithuanian population in 2001–2021: a case‑crossover study
pmc-12706970.creator: Vidmantas Vaičiulis, Ričardas Radišauskas, Olga Meščeriakova, Gintarė Kalinienė, Donatas Valiukas, Laura Seiduanova, Akmaral Abikulova, Jonė Venclovienė
pmc-12706970.description: BackgroundThe creation and implementation of suicide prevention measures requires an evaluation of the full range of potential risk factors. This study examined the associations between the total number of suicides in the season-specific context and various meteorological parameters in Lithuania as a country of the Boreal region.

pmc-12708864.title: RF model and SNA analysis for optimization of regional financial supervision system
pmc-12708864.creator: Tianlei Wei
pmc-12708864.description: As regional financial risks continue to evolve and increasingly intertwine, traditional regulatory frameworks face challenges in timely and accurate risk identification. To address this, the study proposes an optimized regulatory approach that integrates social network analysis (SNA) with a random forest (RF) model.
